title: Onboard artemis-6b-v1.0: perf profiles, metadata, and changelog automation
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds Artemis-6B v1.0 to model registry with curated performance profiles for low/medium/high seq lengths, metadata and tags for runtime selection, and automation to generate changelog entries on release.
description: Context: Onboard Artemis-6B v1.0 as a curated model in the registry. Artemis is a dense 6B model trained for general purpose assistant workloads. This PR adds canonical metadata, performance profiles collected on our cpu/gpu fleet for common sequence length buckets, unit tests, and an update to the changelog generation tooling so releases are automatically surfaced in the registry changelog. Motivation: customers in the mid-market tier have asked for a low-cost, low-latency 6B option with predictable performance characteristics. Having perf profiles encoded in the registry enables smart routing and quantization recommendations in Redwood Optimize. What this PR does (high level): - Add models/artemis/v1.0/metadata.json with model id, architecture, tokenizer, quantization recommendations, licensing, and tags. - Add models/artemis/v1.0/perf_profiles.yaml with throughput and median P50/P95 latency numbers across sequence length buckets (16/128/512) on validated hardware SKUs. - Add tests/test_artemis_profile.py to validate profile schema and plausibility checks. - Update scripts/changelog-generator.py to pick up model registry metadata changes and produce a registry changelog entry under docs/models/CHANGELOG.md. - Add docs/models/artemis.md with usage notes and recommended runtime configs. - Minor CI updates to run the perf profile schema validator on PRs touching models/. Checklist: - [x] Metadata conforms to registry schema (validated by tests) - [x] Perf profiles generated from dedicated perf runs (see commit notes) - [x] Changelog automation updated and unit-tested - [x] Docs added and linked - [x] QA: lightweight smoke-run on dedicated staging cluster (throughput sanity ok) Compatibility notes: Artemis v1.0 is compatible with existing runtime variants. Recommended default: use quantized int4 profile for Dedicated capacity; fallback to fp16 on Hosted when int4 not available. See docs/models/artemis.md for runtime knobs. Migration/rollout: No breaking change. The model is additive and gated behind the registry catalog; Ops can toggle visibility via the catalog flag. Related: ENG-1982 (perf-runbook), PM-457 (customer request), see internal notes in Linear. Manual steps performed: - Perf runs executed on perf-canary cluster using run_perf.py with fixed seed and representative prompts - Changelog generator tested locally and against staging registry Example usage: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/artemis-v1.0/generate -d '{"prompt":"Explain Redwood Optimize in one paragraph"}'
